text:
The operator components are the Pauli matrices multiplied by \(\hbar/2\):
\[
P_i=\frac{\hbar}{2}\sigma_i .
\]

For a direction \(\vec n\) lying in the \(x\!-\!z\) plane we can write  
\[
\vec n=(\sin\theta,0,\cos\theta),
\]
so the operator along \(\vec n\) is  

\[
\vec P\!\cdot\!\vec n=\frac{\hbar}{2}\bigl(\sigma_x\sin\theta+\sigma_z\cos\theta\bigr).
\]

The eigenvalue equation for the eigenvalue \(+\hbar/2\) reduces to  

\[
\bigl(\sigma_x\sin\theta+\sigma_z\cos\theta\bigr)\,|\chi_+\rangle = |\chi_+\rangle .
\]

Writing the Pauli matrices,
\[
\sigma_x=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\sigma_z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},
\]
the matrix to diagonalise is  

\[
M=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\theta & \sin\theta\\ \sin\theta & -\cos\theta\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Solving \((M-I)\,|\chi_+\rangle=0\) gives (up to an overall phase)

\[
|\chi_+\rangle =\begin{pmatrix}\cos(\theta/2)\\ \sin(\theta/2)\end{pmatrix}.
\]

The vector is already normalized (\(\cos^2\frac{\theta}{2}+\sin^2\frac{\theta}{2}=1\)). No extra \(\hbar\) factors appear in the spinor components.

Thus the normalized eigenvector corresponding to eigenvalue \(+\hbar/2\) is  

\[
\boxed{\bigl(\cos(\theta/2),\; \sin(\theta/2)\bigr)^{\!T}}.
\]

This matches option **(B)**.

**Answer: B**
